payload.body: Linguistic register is the map of the system of situationally differentiated language varieties a speech community develops and maintains — the varieties a community deploys for different communicative situations (colloquial, formal, technical, ceremonial, professional) — carved along three parameters. (1) The situational axis: the dimensions along which the varieties are organized are field (the subject matter and activity in which the language is deployed), tenor (the social relations and roles between participants), and mode (the channel and the participatory structure of the discourse); a variety is a conventionalized set of lexical, grammatical, and prosodic choices indexed to the situation, so that the same speaker deploys different varieties in different situations. (2) The boundary lines that separate the map from its neighbours: register is indexed to situation, which distinguishes it from dialect (indexed to region and social group) and from genre (a type of discourse text rather than a variety of the language itself); and it is distinct from the institutional register — an official list maintained by an authority with legal or institutional force — in that a linguistic register is updated by the speech community's convention, not by institutional mandate, and no authority stands behind its entries. (3) The map, not the territory: the entry names the systematic description the community and the discipline build over the natural variation of speech — the inventory of varieties and the dimensions that organize it — not the natural variation itself. Persistence: the varieties persist as social convention — acquired in socialization, maintained through institutional reinforcement (courts, academies, professions, liturgy), and relearned by each generation; the map persists as the stable sub-field of linguistics called register analysis, its dimensions codified in textbooks and corpora. [formal: regiter linguae | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.05]

INSTANCE_OF runs specific to its nearest accepted kind (Law 9), and the nearest kind of a syntactic rule system is not grammar. Per the accepted carves, grammar is the WHOLE — the complete rule system of a language, explicitly including the syntactic, morphological, phonological, and semantic portions — and syntax is a component part of that whole. Whole is not an instance of its own component; the pinned narrowing does not hold.

Changed from STRIKE to ADVANCE on the better argument. I had read the target as a map over natural territory and treated the note's removal as applied to the territory; that was the wrong grain. The accepted definition carves the CATEGORY: 'the human-constructed category for the set of mental processes — perception, memory, reasoning, problem-solving, and attention.' Strip the category and the discipline loses its object: its questions ('how does the mind process sentences?'), its experimental interpretations, and its identity all stand or fall with the category; what remains is the genus (general/behavioral linguistics), not the discipline. That is an operational stop, not a partial loss — my earlier 'the territory remains' point proves too little, because the natural processes that remain are not the discipline's objects; the objects are the categorized processes. The target's accepted definition carves discourse as 'a conventionally structured form of human communication' — its constitutive parameters (communicative context; turn-taking, topic management, and evidentiary standards organizing contributions into a coherent exchange) are activities of the communication process. Removal test: take away the transmission of information between parties and there is no exchange left for discourse's conventions to structure; discourse ceases to operate. This is not bare identity: discourse is not coextensive with communication — it adds the relevance/tone/register/genre conventions ON the transmission process, so it is a form built on a substrate, and removing the substrate removes the form. The board has already accepted the same shape in communication DEPENDS_ON language (remove the encoding system, the transmission process stops) — and the fit is tighter here, since discourse is defined AS a form of communication while communication is only partly linguistic. Kind-membership and mechanism-dependency are not mutually exclusive: the board holds both for language (language INSTANCE_OF communication and communication DEPENDS_ON language are both accepted).

The target's accepted definition carves morphology as a discipline studying 'the internal structure of words and the systematic relations among word-forms', with domain 'the word as a structured unit'. The lexicon's accepted definition is the systematically organized inventory of words, phrases, and meanings a language maintains. Removal test: remove the lexicon and words, word-forms, and the morphemes that build them vanish, so morphology's domain — the internal structure of words — ceases and the discipline loses its object of study. This is the board's own accepted standard for exactly this discipline: morphology DEPENDS_ON lexeme and morphology DEPENDS_ON morpheme both stand. The lexicon is the maintained inventory of those same items, so the dependency on the inventory is the same dependency at the collective level, not a new kind of appeal — and it is not a generic 'X needs language' L8b claim, since the lexicon is a specific part of language, not language as vehicle.

Pinned-sense failure (Law 11d). The target's accepted definition carves phonology as 'a human-made discipline of linguistics that studies the sound systems of languages' — a subfield with its own domain boundary (phoneme inventories, allophones, phonotactics, assimilation, stress, tone), and the board already records that subfield relation as linguistics CONTAINS phonology (accepted). A discipline is a framework for studying a system, not a component inside the system it studies: the grammar system does govern phoneme-level combination (the grammar definition spans 'phonemes into morphemes'), so part of the discipline's domain overlaps grammar's scope — but the discipline as such, including its descriptive inventories and allophonic variation, is not literally a part within the rule system. Contrast the accepted grammar CONTAINS syntax: there syntax is carved as 'the system of rules and conventions... which specifies well-formedness' — a subsystem of rules, a genuine component of the grammar architecture. The filer conflates 'grammar's scope includes the phoneme level' with 'the discipline of phonology is part of grammar'. The sister discipline morphology is treated on this board as a discipline (INSTANCE_OF linguistics; DEPENDS_ON its objects), never as part of grammar — phonology gets the same treatment.

payload.body: Lexeme is a human-made conceptual category — the minimal meaningful unit of a language that functions as the basic item in the mental lexicon of speakers. Three parameters carve the construct: (1) minimal meaningfulness: the lexeme carries semantic content that cannot be decomposed into smaller meaningful parts within that language's grammar, distinguishing it from phrases or complex words whose meaning is compositional; (2) identity-independence: the lexeme has a single abstract identity across all its surface forms — inflectional variants (walk/walks/walked/walking) and allomorphic variants (happy/happiness) express the same lexeme, while a shift in core meaning or derivational structure marks a different lexeme; (3) mental reality: lexemes are stored and retrieved by speakers as discrete units in the mental lexicon, not as lists of word forms. Lexemes persist as the atomic referent of grammatical description, lexical semantics, and word-formation rules. [formal: lexema | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Neurolinguistics is a human-made interdisciplinary field — the study of the neural and biological mechanisms that underlie language acquisition, processing, representation, and comprehension. Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the explanatory level is biological/neural (brain anatomy, neural circuits, electrophysiological responses, neuroimaging data, lesion studies, and molecular markers), not purely behavioral or computational; (2) the phenomenon explained is language in its full range — phonology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, lexicon, acquisition, and breakdown — treated as operations implemented by neural systems. Neurolinguistics persists as an active research enterprise that generates testable hypotheses about how the brain implements language, uses these hypotheses to interpret clinical conditions (aphasia, dyslexia, speech disorders), and informs brain-computer interfaces for language restoration. Paradigmatic methods: fMRI and EEG mapping of language tasks, lesion-symptom mapping in aphasia patients, intracranial electrophysiology, and computational modeling of neural language processing. [formal: neurolinguistica | substrate: brain | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Cognitive-linguistics is a human-made approach to linguistics — the study of language as a manifestation of general cognitive abilities, including categorization, conceptualization, metaphorical reasoning, and embodied experience. Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the explanatory framework denies that language operates as an autonomous module separate from general cognition; language structure reflects domain-general cognitive mechanisms like attention, memory, pattern recognition, and conceptual blending; (2) the empirical evidence comes from cross-linguistic analysis of how semantic structure, syntactic patterns, and figurative language systematically reflect cognitive universals (spatial reasoning, embodiment, force-dynamics) rather than language-internal formal rules. Cognitive-linguistics persists as a theoretical framework that produces models of construction grammar, conceptual metaphor theory, and cognitive semantics, generating testable predictions about language use, acquisition, and processing that compete with modularist accounts. Paradigmatic cases: conceptual metaphor analysis (e.g., ARGUMENT IS WAR), construction grammar descriptions, image-schema theory. [formal: cognitio-linguistica | substrate: mind | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Corpus-linguistics is a human-made empirical approach to linguistics — the study of language patterns, structures, and usage through systematic analysis of large, representative collections of real-language data (corpora). Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the primary data source is authentic, naturally occurring language recorded in written or spoken form (not introspective or constructed examples), organized into annotated or searchable text collections that sample from defined populations, registers, genres, or time periods; (2) the analytical methods are data-driven and statistical, including frequency analysis, collocation measurement, concordance line examination, n-gram modeling, and distributional semantics, used to discover patterns that may not be predictable from theory alone. Corpus-linguistics persists as a methodological framework that generates empirical descriptions of language (dictionaries, grammars), tests theoretical hypotheses against real usage data, and produces applications in language technology (spell checkers, machine translation, language models), lexicography, and language education. Paradigmatic cases: Brown Corpus frequency analysis, COCA/COHA diachronic corpora, Sketch Engine collocation tools. [formal: corpus-linguistica | substrate: data | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Text-linguistics is a human-made discipline of linguistics — the study of the structure, coherence, and function of extended texts (discourses) as structured wholes that extend beyond the sentence level. Two parameters carve the construct: (1) the unit of analysis is the text or discourse as an integrated semantic-pragmatic entity, governed by relations of cohesion (grammatical and lexical ties across clauses), coherence (understandable logical and semantic connections), and communicative purpose (the function the text serves in interaction); (2) the analytical tools include discourse structure analysis (narrative, argumentative, expository patterns), information structure (theme-rheme, given-new), referential continuity (pronoun chains, anaphora resolution), and textual genre conventions that organize texts for specific communicative situations. Text-linguistics persists as a discipline that produces descriptions of textual organization across languages, models of discourse interpretation, and applications in text technology, rhetoric, discourse analysis, and language pedagogy. Paradigmatic cases: Halliday and Hasan's cohesion analysis, van Dijk's discourse semantics, rhetorical structure theory. [formal: textus-linguistica | substrate: mind | horizon: decades | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.note: Removal test (Law 8b): formant-tracking, per its accepted definition, is 'a computational method that estimates the time-varying resonant frequencies of the vocal tract from speech signals by detecting spectral peaks in successive analysis frames.' Its object of operation is the formant itself — the vocal-tract resonant frequency band, per formant's accepted definition ('a peak in spectral energy produced when the vocal tract acts as an acoustic filter'). Remove formant — the resonance that produces the trackable spectral peaks — and formant-tracking stops operating: the peak-picking has nothing to lock onto and the output (the time-varying resonant-frequency contour) ceases to exist. Not mere sayability: the method's mechanism presupposes the resonant band as the structure it measures. payload.body: A cepstrum is the power spectrum of the log-power spectrum of a signal. Computed by: taking the Fourier transform of the signal, computing the log of the magnitude spectrum, then computing the inverse Fourier transform of the log-magnitude spectrum. Parameters: window size for the initial transform, overlap for overlap-add reconstruction. The cepstrum separates periodic structures in the spectrum (such as formant echoes in speech or pitch harmonics) into distinct peaks at quefrency positions corresponding to the delay between reflections. Persistence mechanism: the cepstrum is computed as a deterministic mathematical transform, implemented in speech analysis and audio processing software, and used as an intermediate representation in cepstral feature extraction pipelines. [formal: cepstrum | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Built to persist as a standard auditory model in speech science, psychoacoustics, and audio processing.

payload.note: Cepstrum (the quefrency-domain concept) is derived from the Fourier transform — it is a direct descendant operation: applying the Fourier transform, taking the log of the spectrum, and inverting via a second Fourier-like operation. The Fourier transform is the historical and operational ancestor of cepstral analysis. This is a DERIVED_FROM (historical origin) relation, not DEPENDS_ON.

Remove signal-processing and speech-processing loses its operational techniques: no FFT, no filter design, no spectral analysis — the discipline has no computational mechanisms left. This is an operational dependency, not a generic "every entry needs X" appeal: signal-processing is the specific methodological substrate named in the definition.

The cepstrum as a quefrency-domain CONCEPT was derived from signal-processing practice. Bogert, Healy and Tukey invented cepstral analysis specifically to address signal-processing needs (detecting periodic structures in spectra for speech analysis). The concept of quefrency-domain representation was derived from and named after the signal-processing operations (FFT, log, IFFT) that produce it. Which-came-first: signal-processing methods and needs existed first; the cepstrum concept was derived from them.

SERVES asks for whose sake (Law 8d): servant->master. Prosody's accepted definition carves it as 'the constructed linguistic framework for analyzing rhythmic, stress, and intonational patterns in spoken language,' persisting through phonetic transcription, linguistic pedagogy, and metrical theory — its purpose is the analysis of prosodic structure in language, not service to any sister discipline. The note inverts the actual relationship: phonetics' own accepted definition fixes its method as 'measurement and cross-linguistic description — articulatory geometry, acoustic values such as formants and spectrograms, and perceptual classification.' It is phonetic measurement that supplies the raw values (pitch contour, loudness, duration) which prosodic analysis then organizes — the master uses the servant's output, not the reverse. A framework built to analyze patterns in spoken language is not built for the sake of the discipline that measures its inputs. The direction, if any, would run from measurement toward prosodic analysis, not from prosody toward phonetics.

Removal test (Law 8b): remove signal-processing — the discipline whose accepted definition carves 'mathematical transforms (Fourier, wavelet, cepstral), filtering operations, and computational algorithms' — and speech-processing loses its operational machinery. Its own accepted definition names the representation domain: time-domain waveform, short-time Fourier transform, mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, linear prediction coefficients. Every one of those representations is a signal-processing construct: the STFT is windowing plus FFT, MFCCs are a cepstrum of a mel-warped spectrum, LPC is a prediction filter. No FFT, no filter design, no spectral estimation, no windowed analysis — the discipline's toolkits (HTK, Kaldi, librosa) are DSP libraries. The scope itself calls it 'a human-made signal-processing discipline.' This is not the generic 'every entry needs signals' appeal: the substrate is specific, named in the definition's own parameters, and its removal leaves the task objectives (intelligibility improvement, speaker identification) without any computational mechanism to pursue them. The board already accepts the parallel structure (speech-intelligibility DEPENDS_ON speech-processing, now pending in reverse) and a dozen X DEPENDS_ON signal-processing edges of the same shape.

SERVES test (Law 8d, for whose sake, servant->master) passes cleanly on the pinned sense. Language-variety's accepted scope calls it 'a human-made analytical genus of sociolinguistics ... built to persist as the discipline's instrument for sorting dialects, idiolects, and their kin,' and its definition states the persistence mechanism explicitly: 'the genus persists as an instrument of the discipline — codified in sociolinguistic research and teaching ... it is the made scaffold that makes dialect and idiolect comparable units of one science.' The genus is the servant (an instrument of sorting), sociolinguistics is the master (the discipline for whose sake the sorting exists). The definition does not merely tolerate this reading — it asserts it in those terms. Contrast the failing case: a framework whose purpose is its own domain of analysis (prosody analyzing prosodic structure) does not serve the disciplines that measure its inputs; a genus defined as 'the discipline's instrument' does serve that discipline. The note pins exactly the sense the definition carves, and judges judge the pinned sense (Law 11d).

Removal test (Law 8b) on the pinned sense: the accepted definition carves the glottal-source model as 'the periodic excitation generated by vocal fold vibration,' with parameters fundamental frequency, open quotient, asymmetry coefficient, return phase. F0's accepted definition carves the lowest frequency of a periodic waveform — the rate at which the source repeats its cycle — persisting through estimation algorithms (YIN, pYIN) and pitch-tracking conventions. Remove F0 and the model loses its defining parameter: the excitation it exists to specify is periodic excitation, and a period without a rate is an un-specifiable period. The other parameters do not rescue it — open quotient is a fraction of the glottal cycle, and asymmetry and return phase are measured in fractions of that same cycle; they are shape parameters RELATIVE to the cycle whose length is 1/F0. Without F0 the pulse has no clock, and the model cannot specify which voice it produces. The carved sense is the periodic source (aperiodic sources live elsewhere in the source-filter framework), and within that sense F0 is constitutive, not incidental. The board has already accepted two edges of this exact parameter-constituency shape pointing at fundamental-frequency.

Two failures, either fatal. (1) Sense mismatch (Law 11d): the filed target is speech-processing, whose accepted definition carves a signal-processing discipline — 'implemented as software toolkits (HTK, Kaldi, librosa), DSP libraries, and neural network models,' persisted through repositories, benchmarks, and commercial APIs. The note's removal test, however, deletes 'the cognitive mechanism for perceiving, producing, and interpreting speech' — a natural human capacity that no live entry holds. The test was run against the territory, not against the filed map. (2) Generic appeal (Law 8b): 'prosody operates only through spoken language' is the overstatement true of every mind/behavior-substrate entry and files nothing. Apply the test to the actual target: remove the speech-processing discipline (the engineering field of speech technology) and prosody — 'the constructed linguistic framework for analyzing rhythmic, stress, and intonational patterns,' persisting 'through phonetic transcription, linguistic pedagogy, and metrical theory' — keeps operating exactly as before: its transcriptions, metrical analyses, and classroom teaching do not require HTK or Kaldi to stand. Chronology confirms the direction is backwards: prosodic analysis in linguistics predates speech processing as a technology field by decades. A dependency on a natural capacity is not a dependency on the filed discipline.

The correct binding for this word is the suprasegment entry, and labels use STRIKE-then-file-the-correction, so this one falls.

payload.body: A sociolect is a variety of language associated with a particular social group or social class, distinguished by systematic conventions in lexicon, pronunciation, and grammar that mark group membership. It operates through shared linguistic practices that emerge from common social experiences, institutional affiliations, or cultural positions — distinct from dialects (which are geographic) and registers (which are situational). Parameters include the social boundary that defines the group (occupation, education level, socioeconomic status, subculture), the degree of linguistic convergence or divergence from the broader vernacular, and the social indexicality of distinctive forms. Persistence mechanism: sociolects persist as living practice within groups — reproduced through social interaction, reinforced through identity marking, and maintained through the group's internal need for linguistic solidarity, independent of any formal codification or institutional support. [formal: sociolectus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.50]

payload.name: intonation
payload.scope: Intonation is the human-constructed linguistic dimension of pitch organization in speech: the systematic, rule-governed framework by which utterances use rising and falling pitch to carry grammar, focus, and attitude — built to be transcribed, taught, and analyzed across generations of speakers and linguists.

payload.scope: Intonation is the human-constructed linguistic dimension of pitch organization in speech: the systematic, rule-governed framework by which utterances use rising and falling pitch to carry grammar, focus, and attitude — built to be transcribed, taught, and analyzed across generations of speakers and linguists.

payload.body: Intonation is the constructed linguistic framework for analyzing pitch-contour organization in spoken language: the way fundamental frequency rises and falls across the duration of an utterance, and the way those movements are patterned by linguistic rule rather than speaker whim. Parameters: (1) pitch contour - the F0 trajectory across the utterance, rising, falling, or level; (2) tone unit - the stretch of speech over which a single contour operates, delimited by pauses; (3) nuclear stress - the syllable carrying the principal tone of the tone unit; (4) grammatical and attitudinal function - contour used to mark clause type (interrogative vs declarative), focus, and attitude (e.g., English rising terminals for yes-no questions). Persistence: intonation is realized in every produced utterance, analyzed in intonation notation (e.g., ToBI), taught in language pedagogy, and studied in phonology; it persists as long as speech carries meaning through pitch. [formal: intonatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Stress is the constructed phonological framework for analyzing prominence asymmetry within words and phrases: certain syllables are marked as stressed (more prominent) relative to their neighbors, and this marking is patterned by linguistic rule. Parameters: (1) degree - relative prominence against neighbors, primary and secondary; (2) realization - the cue bundle carrying stress: increased loudness, increased duration, and, in English, pitch height on the stressed syllable; (3) position - placement within the word, rule-governed in many languages and capable of distinguishing word identity (English 'record' noun vs verb); (4) phrase level - the organization of stresses into rhythmic groups in connected speech. Persistence: stress is realized in every utterance, transcribed in phonology, taught in phonetics and language pedagogy, and codified in dictionaries; it persists as a stable parameter of the linguistic system, changing only slowly across generations. [formal: stressum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Accent is the constructed sociolinguistic concept for the phonological component of a speech variety: the distinctive sound patterns by which a listener identifies a speaker's regional or social origin, in the absence of lexical or grammatical difference. Parameters: (1) phonemic inventory - the distinctive vowel and consonant qualities of the accent; (2) articulation - characteristic manner and place of production; (3) prosodic coloring - the intonational and rhythmic quality that colors the accent; (4) indexing - the geographic and social identity the accent signals to listeners. Accent is the phonological part of dialect: dialect is the whole (phonology + lexicon + grammar), and a speaker can be described by the accent alone while sharing the full dialect. Persistence: accent persists in the speech communities that produce it, is transmitted through first-language acquisition and socialization, and is indexed in dialect atlases and sociolinguistic study; it persists as a stable social marker in individual speakers. [formal: accentus | substrate: language | horizon: generations | explicit: no | epoch: 0.4]

payload.scope: An utterance is the human-constructed concept for a contiguous stretch of speech or writing treated by its participants as a single unit of communicative action. Built to persist through transcription conventions, dialogue annotation systems, and the analytical frameworks of pragmatics and discourse analysis that parse continuous language use into tractable units.

payload.body: An utterance is the human-constructed concept for a contiguous stretch of speech or writing that participants in a communicative event treat as a single, bounded unit of action. Parameters: (1) physical extent — the actual span of vocal articulation or written symbols, from first sound/symbol to last; (2) communicative boundary — the participants' shared understanding of where this unit begins and ends, which may diverge from grammatical boundaries (an utterance may span multiple sentences or be a fragment of one); (3) functional unit — the utterance performs some recoverable communicative function within the ongoing interaction. Distinction from related constructs: a sentence is a grammatical unit defined by syntactic rules; a speech act is the action performed by an utterance (one utterance may realize multiple speech acts); discourse is the larger organized structure of multiple utterances. Persistence: maintained through transcription conventions, dialogue annotation frameworks, and the analytical practices of pragmatics and discourse analysis. [formal: uterantia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.note: UTTERANCE is defined as a unit that 'performs some recoverable communicative function within the ongoing interaction.' A speech act IS a communicative function. The concept of utterance as a communicative unit (not merely a physical span of speech) is only meaningful through the speech acts it realizes. Removal test: remove speech act and the utterance loses its functional dimension, becoming just a physical event rather than a concept of communicative action. Direction: utterance depends on speech act; speech act concept operates independently of any specific utterance. This is the functional dimension that distinguishes utterance from mere phonation or text span.

payload.body: Accent is the sociolinguistic category that isolates the phonological component of a speech variety as an independently indexable unit: the sound patterns by which a listener identifies a speaker's regional or social origin, abstracted from lexical and grammatical difference. Parameters: (1) isolation rule — the map draws its boundary by holding lexicon and grammar constant and varying only the phonological system (the 'same words, different sound' test); (2) indexed content — the origin the category encodes: regional (e.g., Scots, Geordie, Australian) or social (e.g., RP, AAVE); (3) descriptive levels the map organizes — phonemic inventory, articulation, prosodic coloring; (4) contrast frame — an accent is defined against a reference variety within the same language. Persistence: the category is maintained as an instrument of the discipline — dialect atlases (Survey of English Dialects), sociolinguistic textbooks and curricula, accent-labeling practice in media and pedagogy, and listening-identification tests — drawn, taught, and revised by sociolinguists; it is maintained by the discipline, not transmitted by speakers. payload.note: CONTAINS = part-of: the variety is the whole, the accent is a constituent part. Dialect's accepted definition carves a variety as a bundle of component systems: '(1) phonological — distinctive sound patterns and pronunciation conventions; (2) lexical; (3) grammatical; (4) social index.' The phonological component of a variety is exactly what the accent category names: a dialect decomposes into accent ⊕ lexicon ⊕ grammar, and dialect atlases perform precisely this decomposition. Contrast with the struck prosody CONTAINS stress: there prosody is an analytic framework and stress a dimension it measures — analytic relation, not constituent. Here the relation is constitutive: a speaker can be characterized by accent alone while sharing the full dialect (the definition's own test), and the component is independently indexable — taught, tested, and atlased on its own. Pinned sense (Law 11d): accent as the phonological component of a variety per its isolation rule (same words, different sound).

Removal test (Law 8b) against the filed carve: utterance is 'a contiguous stretch of speech or writing treated by its participants as a single, bounded unit of communicative action' — a unit of the sign system. Remove language (the system of signs) and the stretch of speech or writing is no longer a sign-event: what remains is vocalization or ink marks, and no unit of communicative action can be treated, transcribed, or annotated, because treating a stretch as a communicative unit requires that the stretch SAY something. The construct stops operating, not merely stops being sayable. Same accepted shape as speech-act DEPENDS_ON language (accepted: 'utterances as meaningful sign-events no longer exist — what remains is acoustic or gestural behavior without illocutionary force') and discourse DEPENDS_ON language. Direction: the utterance-unit needs language; language operates without the notion of an utterance-unit. Pinned sense: utterance as bounded unit of communicative action within the sign system, not mere physical span.

Remove utterance now — the unit participants treat as a single bounded unit of action, which the discipline transcribes and segments — and the speech act has no bearer to be an act OF: an action performed by an utterance is not an act performed by a bare span of sound or ink. The pragmatic framework stops classifying, because illocutionary force is force OF a unit, not of a continuum. Direction check (Law 8c): the converse fails — utterance operates without the speech-act taxonomy (a stretch is a bounded unit of action whether or not anyone classifies its illocutionary force), which is exactly why utterance DEPENDS_ON speech-act runs the wrong way and should fall.
